data.narrative:
Hyperscale Power is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Rothmund (PhD ETH Zurich, ex-ABB) and Sami Pettersson (ex-ABB), having raised €5M to date. The target operates within a fragmented peer universe of 9 same-sector companies, comprising 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Traditional peer-median valuation proves inapplicable due to insufficient clustering at the seed stage within Climate & Energy. No three or more comparables aligned on stage, proximity, or valuation tier, rendering a narrow peer multiple approach unreliable. A broad sector-median method would obscure stage-specific and business-model differences material to seed-stage risk assessment. The single public comparable (LNZA) operates at a different maturity level, limiting direct benchmarking utility.

Without sufficient peer triangulation, this valuation lacks a quantitative anchor. The analysis would require either: (1) expansion to adjacent cleantech stages to establish minimum valuation bands; (2) application of founder pedigree and capital efficiency metrics (€5M deployed by experienced materials and energy professionals from ABB); or (3) bottom-up revenue projection models tied to addressable market sizing. The key uncertainty remains the lack of comparable seed-stage exits or public trading multiples in the narrow Climate & Energy frontier-tech segment, making any point estimate speculative without additional fundamental build-up.
